badge.$comment: A word wearing a tone (0053). The box is text-sized — a badge stands on no control axis, because it is not a control — and every tone is one bg/fg/border triple: `neutral` is the base with no suffix (the `md` rule, on the tone axis), `danger` the first variant, and the union in `PctBadgeTone` grows the day the skin grows ramps for the rest. The border is drawn under every tone for the forced-colours reason the chips wrote down: the fill is the first thing every flattening takes.
badge.$comment-radius: `radius.md` and deliberately not the chips' pill: a chip LOOKS grabbable because it is, and a word of status must not borrow that costume — the corner is the one visual cue telling the scanning eye which small box answers the pointer.

gap.$description: Gap between the badge's text and its icon.

badge.$comment-danger: The skin's error colour painting its first background — the return `semantic.light.json` promised, with `on-danger` as the word over it. The border is the same colour as the fill on purpose: the edge exists for the modes that drop the fill, and in the author palette it simply thickens the box by nothing.

bg-danger.$description: Background of the badge in the danger tone.

fg-danger.$description: Text colour of the badge in the danger tone.

border-danger.$description: Edge colour of the badge in the danger tone.
